walkthroughs.body_html:
Debussy blurred harmonic rules with whole-tone and pentatonic scales, parallel chords and washy pedalled piano. His Clair de lune (1905) evokes moonlight rather than telling a story.

This was the start of breaking away from Romantic certainty — colour and atmosphere over tonal direction.

The 1913 premiere of The Rite of Spring caused an audience riot. Stravinsky used pounding polyrhythms, savage dissonance and constantly changing time signatures.

It signalled that 20th-century music would explore rhythm and primal energy as much as harmony.

Schoenberg abandoned keys altogether, then invented twelve-tone serialism — every piece based on an ordered row of all 12 pitches.

Later in the century, minimalists Steve Reich and Philip Glass reacted with steady pulses, repeating cells and gradual change — the opposite of complexity for its own sake.
